tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, Prerequisite check; Behavior bullets 1-3, 6 (People store) and the widened predicate in bullet 4; Required behavior: Roles and the permission matrix, Target rules, Where the role is checked, The 403 page, Two-factor requirement, Database and People log; Acceptance evidence 1, 3, 6 (predicate), 8 (append-only store), 10 and existing-route portions of 2. Before any edit, verify merged console main contains #563's TOTP migration and enrolment route. If absent, request needs-input naming #563 and change nothing. If own password change, the organisation requirement or owner recovery already exists, reuse it and request the specified hold for that part. Record the #563 SHA, previous schema and baseline full-test elapsed time. Do not implement #563 cryptography or session UI. Add migration N after the actual latest migration without editing earlier SQL: role triggers, require_2fa_all default 0, invites, reset_links and append-only people_events with exactly the specified columns, constraints and delete behavior. Read and narrow actual stored roles; preserve existing Owner/password/session/factor data and newer-schema errors. Implement the complete 27-row policy, target rules, required-role messages and the two extra actions; future screens remain policy-only. Add the typed appendPeopleEvent interface and durable snapshots, usable inside callers' transactions and later token actions. Integrate the live TOTP predicate with #563's gate, including its existing account-security routes; if the prerequisite gate lives elsewhere, change only its call/export as the plan permits and name that real module in the PR. Declare guards for every currently registered app route, preserve ops behavior, implement existing-route GET/POST order and role-aware 403, and make the route test reject undeclared registrations. Later tasks extend that literal route test when registering their routes. Do not expose unfinished team/link routes or dead navigation. Update README/configuration alongside these changes. This task is one foundation seam because migration, typed role reads, policy and the live gate must agree before any non-owner can be created.

tasks.title: Owners and admins can manage permitted people with atomic People events
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, Behavior bullets 3-6 and 9 for Team listing, role changes, removal, administrative 2FA reset, ownership transfer and team.require-2fa; Required behavior: Routes for those operations, 2FA reset of another person, Role change, Removal, Ownership transfer, Two-factor requirement, People log and Pages, metrics and logs; Acceptance evidence 2 rows 16-19,23-25 plus team.view/team.require-2fa, 3, 6-8 and 11 for these pages; Counterexamples Roles, Ids, Stale state, Transfer sessions, Promotion, Transfer, Removal and People log. Depends on T1. Wire the real team store and prerequisite factor-removal dependency from main.ts; preserve startup and shutdown behavior and existing test dependency injection. Implement server-rendered /team and its people/pending-list data, adding invite/reset controls only when their handlers land in T3/T4. Add the guarded role/remove/reset-2fa/transfer/require-2fa routes and landing Team link, id/role/confirmation validation and responsive forms. Every mutation re-reads actor and target inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE and writes its People event atomically; failures roll back and return the specified safe 500. Role changes end every target session; 2FA reset deletes factors/recovery material and every target session. Removal preserves history, cascades account links/sessions/factors, invalidates invites by removed issuers and requires the trimmed exact typed name. Transfer only to a TOTP-enrolled Admin: demote old Owner before promoting target, delete every session of both people including requester, delete response cookie and redirect /sign-in?transfer=done with the specified notice. Recheck concurrent/stale state. Implement Owner-only require-2fa with its event and live gate. Include the API-token warning in removal and document that Full access stays A+, canGrant bounds grants by the shared token's scopes, API cannot identify Console people and removal does not revoke API tokens. Add safe committed-change logs and canonical path labels for these routes as they become active. Keep docs/endpoints current and publish docs/team.md with the unchanged matrix and the later-screen registration/person-log handoff. These user-management operations share actor/target transaction rules and confirmation pages, so they stay together.

tasks.title: Copied invitations expire in seven days and create the bound account once
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, Behavior invite portions of bullets 3,5,6,9; Required behavior: Invites, invite Routes, Link origin, anonymous public-link GET/POST order and Pages, metrics and logs; Acceptance evidence 2 rows 14-15, 3-4, 4a for invite, 4b for existing-session acceptance, 6 for invite enrolment, 8 and 11; all Invite and invite Paths Counterexamples, and Session cookie on link routes. Depends on T1/T2. Add shared 32-byte base64url token generation, SHA-256 hex digest, raw-path parsing for invite/reset tokens and origin-based link building. Do not enable reset routes until T4. Implement normalized bound email/role, one live invite per email, account conflict, seven-day expiry, pending/expired list, authorized revocation and issuer-authority validity. Add create/revoke/accept People transactions with rollback and rechecks, atomic one-use concurrency and invalid-form retry. Links are copied by hand once in a read-only input and text; no SMTP/email. Add public GET/POST /invite/<token> with no session or role step: valid GET ensures/reuses the anonymous CSRF cookie, invalid GET sets none, POST validates Origin/form/anonymous cookie before lookup and KDF, then validates fields and commits. A session cookie is irrelevant to these public guards. Use the fixed email/role, ignoring extra acceptance fields. Only after the invite commit has succeeded, read the request's session cookie for rotation: delete the row it names even if it belongs to the issuing Admin or any other user, then create and return exactly the new user's session. Unknown/expired session cookies do not prevent acceptance; failed validation or commit must not delete the old session. Start a fresh session as at sign-in only after successful acceptance; route invited Admin and organisation-required Member/Viewer through #563 enrolment before protected use. Preserve the public-origin/validated-loopback rules and ignore forwarded headers. Add canonical /invite/:token metrics, invalid raw paths labelled other, safe committed logs, no-store and unchanged CSP/referrer policy. Update route guard literals, docs, layout and leak tests with this behavior. The helper, lifecycle, anonymous form and enrolment continuation stay one task because together they make an invitation usable and safe.

tasks.title: Password changes and one-use resets cannot be undone by stale credential work
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, reset/own-password portions of Behavior bullets 3,5,6,7,9; Required behavior: Password reset links, Own password, Credential changes during password work, their Routes, public-link GET/POST order, People log and Pages, metrics and logs; Acceptance evidence 2 rows 20-22,27, 3, 4a for reset, 4b for the reset session cookie, 5, 5a, 8 and 11; Counterexamples Reset time and use, Reset authority, Reset effects, Own password, Credential races, Session cookie on link routes and anonymous reset CSRF. Depends on T3's link helper and T1/T2. Implement copied reset issuance for Member/Viewer by Admin/Owner and Admin by Owner, never Owner through Team. Replace prior unused team links without ending sessions at issue; digest-only storage, 86400000 ms expiry, target-role snapshot and live issuer authority. Public /reset/<token> GET/POST uses the anonymous CSRF cookie exactly as the invite flow, never reads the session cookie and has no session/2FA/role checks; invalid links are checked before KDF and share the invalid-link page. Successful use atomically changes password, consumes the link, removes other unused links and every target session, and logs user.password-reset; retain TOTP/recovery codes and create no session. Implement owner-recovery-kind redemption through the same transaction, clearing factors via #563, logging owner.recover with container actor and forcing enrolment at the next sign-in; T5 supplies its container-only issuer. Add /account/password for all four roles, current-password validation, existing email/client throttle, password bounds, a compare-and-set in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: re-read the request's session row and user, require the session still exists and password_hash still equals H0 read before verification, then change the password, delete every other session and append user.password-change, preserving the current session and factors. A failed compare answers 409 with the literal spec message, changes no row, writes no event and releases the throttle reservation. Pending reset links stay valid after an own password change. Change existing sign-in too: the verified-hash check, deletion of the browser's old session/expired sessions and new session insertion run in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, continuing only if the user still exists and its password_hash equals the verified hash. Revalidation failure is 401 Wrong email or password., counts a throttle failure, logs sign-in failed reason credentials and sets no session cookie, including when removal raced. If #563 has a separate second-factor step, keep the verified hash server-side and apply the check to its final session-creation commit; name any adapted prerequisite module in the PR. Rely on fresh-salted Bun.password.hash rather than password-text comparison. Add password-change auth metrics, /reset/:token and account/team-reset labels, safe logs, password link on landing, sign-in reset notice, responsive no-script pages and current docs. Tests cover invalid-form retry, replacement, stale authority, removed accounts, concurrent use and every deterministic interleaving of acceptance 5a as well as the HTTP matrix. Keep the sign-in race tests in src/server.sign-in.test.ts and the own-password races in src/server.races.test.ts, using injected gated hashPassword/verifier calls and no timers. These credential writes and sign-in session creation share the credential/session transaction boundary; implement them and their race regressions together so reset cannot ship alongside the old sign-in race.
